

### Overlay of merged detection curves {#sec-appendix-sweep-plot}

Each pair's **merged** curve is constructed with the same conventions
as the reference figure (@sec-appendix-detection): corrected
prediction for θ ≤ `r theta_merge_cut` using that pair's own
`L_eff_cal`, uncorrected per-subgroup P1(θ) for θ ≥ `r theta_merge_cut`
using that pair's (c₁, c₂).  The reference pair is drawn with a
heavier line weight; verification diamonds from the theta-grid work
are overlaid at the reference pair only (the other pairs have not
been independently verified — this figure assumes transportability of
the multiplicity correction based on the reference pair's verification).

```{r sweep-plot}
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Merged detection-curve overlay across (c1, c2) sensitivity sweep.  Each pair's curve uses its own L_eff_cal and operational thresholds in the same estimate-then-predict structure as the reference figure.  Verification diamonds shown only at the reference pair (1.25, 1.00).  At θ = 1 each curve's y-value is the simulated FPR for that (c1, c2); at θ > 1 the curve is an interpretable per-subgroup TPR when the harm-subgroup HR equals θ."

theta_seq_sweep <- seq(0.5, 3.0, by = 0.05)

# Build per-pair curve data
sweep_curve_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sweep_results, function(r) {
  # Uncorrected P1 curve at this (c1, c2)
  p1 <- sapply(theta_seq_sweep, function(th)
    tryCatch(
      compute_detection_probability_glm(
        theta = th, d_eff = r$d_eff, c1 = r$c1, c2 = r$c2,
        effect_scale = "ratio", method = "monte_carlo"),
      error = function(e) NA_real_))
  # Corrected prediction
  p_corr <- if (!is.na(r$L_eff)) 1 - (1 - p1)^r$L_eff
            else rep(NA_real_, length(theta_seq_sweep))

  # Merge: corrected for θ ≤ cut, uncorrected for θ ≥ cut (same split
  # used for the reference figure — makes curves visually comparable)
  null_idx <- theta_seq_sweep <= theta_merge_cut
  alt_idx  <- theta_seq_sweep >= theta_merge_cut
  merged <- numeric(length(theta_seq_sweep))
  merged[null_idx] <- p_corr[null_idx]
  merged[alt_idx]  <- p1[alt_idx]

  data.frame(
    theta    = theta_seq_sweep,
    prob     = merged,
    pair     = sprintf("c1 = %.2f, c2 = %.2f", r$c1, r$c2),
    is_ref   = (r$c1 == c1_paper) & (r$c2 == c2_paper)
  )
}))

# Verification diamonds (reference pair only).  Include θ = 1 from the
# reference calibration and any theta_grid_verify points.
ref_diamonds <- data.frame(
  theta = 1, prob = fpr_cal, ci_lo = ci_cal[1], ci_hi = ci_cal[2]
)
if (!is.null(theta_verify_df) && nrow(theta_verify_df) > 0L) {
  ref_diamonds <- rbind(
    ref_diamonds,
    data.frame(theta = theta_verify_df$theta,
               prob  = theta_verify_df$fpr,
               ci_lo = theta_verify_df$ci_lo,
               ci_hi = theta_verify_df$ci_hi)
  )
}

# Per-pair linewidth and alpha: reference pair emphasized
sweep_curve_df$lwd   <- ifelse(sweep_curve_df$is_ref, 1.3, 0.8)
sweep_curve_df$alpha <- ifelse(sweep_curve_df$is_ref, 1.0, 0.85)

ggplot(sweep_curve_df, aes(x = theta, y = prob,
                           colour = pair, group = pair)) +
  # FPR target demarcation line (horizontal) — the analyst's
  # operational budget for procedure-level Type-I error.  Drawn more
  # prominently than the θ = 1 / θ = theta_merge_cut reference lines
  # because it directly indicates which (c1, c2) pairs fall within the
  # target budget vs exceed it.
  geom_hline(yintercept = fpr_target_surv, linetype = "longdash",
             colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  annotate("text",
           x = 0.55, y = fpr_target_surv,
           label = sprintf("FPR target = %.0f%%", 100 * fpr_target_surv),
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 3.2, colour = "firebrick", fontface = "bold") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = theta_merge_cut, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = lwd, alpha = alpha), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_errorbar(data = ref_diamonds,
                aes(x = theta, ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi),
                colour = "black", width = 0.05, linewidth = 0.7,
                inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = ref_diamonds,
             aes(x = theta, y = prob),
             colour = "black", size = 3.5, shape = 18,
             inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.85) +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x      = "True harm-subgroup HR (θ†(H))",
    y      = "Detection probability",
    colour = "(c1, c2)",
    title  = sprintf("(c1, c2) sensitivity sweep | %d pairs × %d sims",
                     nrow(sweep_grid), nsims_sweep),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Diamonds: verification at reference (%.2f, %.2f); merge at θ = %.2f; FPR budget = %.0f%%",
      c1_paper, c2_paper, theta_merge_cut, 100 * fpr_target_surv)
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position        = "inside",                       # ggplot2 >= 3.5.0 idiom
    legend.position.inside = c(0.80, 0.30),                  # right-middle band of panel
    legend.justification    = c(0, 0.5),                      # left-middle anchor of legend
    legend.background       = element_rect(fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.85),
                                           colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.key              = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
    legend.key.size         = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    legend.title            = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text             = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.margin           = margin(4, 6, 4, 6),
    plot.title              = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle           = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30"),
    panel.grid.minor        = element_blank()
  )
```


### Interpretation of the sweep {#sec-appendix-sweep-interp}

**FPR side (left of θ = 1).**  At θ = 1 each curve's y-value is that
pair's simulated FPR under H0, and the range of FPRs across the grid
shows how sensitive the procedure-level Type-I error is to operational
threshold choice.  The reference pair (`r c1_paper`, `r sprintf("%.2f", c2_paper)`)
is one point in this range; tighter thresholds (larger c₁ and/or c₂)
push FPR down, looser thresholds push it up.  The red dashed
horizontal line at `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fpr_target_surv)` marks
the analyst's FPR budget — any pair whose curve lies below this line
at θ = 1 is operating within the target Type-I error rate.

**TPR side (right of θ = 1).**  For each pair, the curve at θ > 1
traces the per-subgroup detection probability (uncorrected P1) when
the harm subgroup's true HR equals θ.  This is the power characteristic
under each (c₁, c₂) configuration for a single subgroup of effective
size d_eff.  Higher curves indicate faster detection of stronger harm
signals.

**Reading the tradeoff.**  A pair that sits uniformly above another is
both more powerful (higher TPR in the alt region) and less
conservative (higher FPR in the null region) — that pair trades
Type-I error for Type-II error.  A pair that dominates another on
both axes (rare but possible when the grid is coarse) is strictly
better.  Ordinarily the curves reveal a Pareto frontier, and the
analyst's job is to choose the point on that frontier consistent with
the trial's error-rate budget.

**Caveats.**  This sweep assumes the multiplicity correction
transports across (c₁, c₂); it has been verified only at the
reference pair.  For production reporting at a non-reference pair,
an analyst should re-run the full tier-1 + verification + theta-grid
workflow at that pair to confirm.  The sweep is a fast exploration
tool, not a substitute for the full appendix workflow.


# Computational Timing {#sec-timing}

```{r timing-summary}
# Helpers (%||%, .fpr_stage, .sec_per_sim) are defined in the main setup
# chunk so they can be QC-tested before any expensive simulation.
timings$total <- (proc.time() - t_vignette_start)["elapsed"]

# FPR appendix sub-components — individual stages plus rolled-up total.
# Each stage may be 0 (skipped via nsims_*_fpr = 0L) or NA (not run at
# all).  Show NA for skipped stages in the table so the reader can tell
# a skip from a fast run.
fpr_tier1_sec  <- .fpr_stage(timings$fpr_runsim)        # calibration batch
fpr_verify_sec <- .fpr_stage(timings$fpr_verify)        # verification batch
fpr_theta_sec  <- .fpr_stage(timings$fpr_theta_verify)  # theta-grid verification
fpr_sweep_sec  <- .fpr_stage(timings$fpr_sweep)         # (c1, c2) sensitivity sweep

timings$fpr_total <- sum(c(fpr_tier1_sec, fpr_verify_sec, fpr_theta_sec,
                           fpr_sweep_sec),
                         na.rm = TRUE)

n_theta_total <- if (!is.null(theta_verify_df))
  sum(theta_verify_df$nsims, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_

n_sweep_total <- if (exists("sweep_df") && !is.null(sweep_df))
  sum(sweep_df$nsims, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_

timing_df <- data.frame(
  Analysis = c("GRF",
               "ForestSearch",
               "Bootstrap",
               "kfold CV",
               "OOB CV",
               "FPR tier 1 (calibration batch)",
               "FPR verification batch",
               "FPR theta-grid verification",
               "FPR (c1, c2) sensitivity sweep",
               "FPR calibration — total (appendix)",
               "Total"),
  Seconds = as.numeric(c(
    timings$grf          %||% NA_real_,
    timings$forestsearch %||% NA_real_,
    timings$bootstrap    %||% NA_real_,
    timings$kfold        %||% NA_real_,
    timings$oob          %||% NA_real_,
    fpr_tier1_sec,
    fpr_verify_sec,
    fpr_theta_sec,
    fpr_sweep_sec,
    if (timings$fpr_total > 0) timings$fpr_total else NA_real_,
    timings$total        %||% NA_real_
  )),
  Sims = c(
    NA_integer_, NA_integer_,
    NB_boot %||% NA_integer_,
    Ksims_cv %||% NA_integer_,
    Ksims_cv %||% NA_integer_,
    nsims_tier1_fpr %||% NA_integer_,
    nsims_verify_fpr %||% NA_integer_,
    n_theta_total,
    n_sweep_total,
    NA_integer_,
    NA_integer_
  )
)
timing_df$Minutes     <- timing_df$Seconds / 60
timing_df$sec_per_sim <- mapply(.sec_per_sim, timing_df$Seconds, timing_df$Sims)

gt(timing_df) |>
  tab_header(title = "Computational Timing") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Seconds, Minutes), decimals = 1,
             rows = !is.na(Seconds)) |>
  fmt_number(columns = sec_per_sim, decimals = 2,
             rows = !is.na(sec_per_sim)) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = Sims, rows = !is.na(Sims)) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  cols_label(
    Analysis    = "Component",
    Seconds     = "Time (sec)",
    Minutes     = "Time (min)",
    Sims        = "Sims",
    sec_per_sim = "sec / sim"
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = Analysis %in% c(
      "FPR calibration — total (appendix)", "Total"))
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#F5F5F5"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = Analysis %in% c(
      "FPR tier 1 (calibration batch)",
      "FPR verification batch",
      "FPR theta-grid verification",
      "FPR (c1, c2) sensitivity sweep"))
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(paste(
    "FPR calibration stages are shaded grey; their sum appears as the",
    "bold 'FPR calibration — total (appendix)' row.",
    "sec/sim divides elapsed time by the simulation count for the",
    "appendix stages and by NB_boot / Ksims_cv for bootstrap / CV.",
    "Dashes indicate skipped or non-simulation components.",
    "When cached stages are loaded from .rds (cache HIT), the elapsed",
    "time shown is from the ORIGINAL run, not the current knit."))
```
